Title: Hard Sorting Strategy Exercise

- test repository: add class `MergeSortEdgeCasesTest` with tests `testMergeSortNullInput` (expects IllegalArgumentException on null input) and `testMergeSortEmpty` (expects no exception and unchanged list)
- test repository: add class `ContextPolicyRobustnessTest` with tests `testContextNoStrategy` (expects IllegalStateException when sort() called without strategy) and `testPolicyNullDates` (expects IllegalArgumentException when configure() called with null dates list)
- problem statement: add a new "Part 4: Harder Requirements" section describing the six additional tasks and their test references
- update PlantUML diagram: no structural changes needed (existing classes already cover new tests)

Invariants:
- the number of original test cases and their names stays identical

- the template repository still compiles but fails the tests

Problem statement:
In this exercise, we want to implement sorting algorithms and choose them based on runtime specific variables.

### Part 1: Sorting

First, we need to implement two sorting algorithms, in this case `MergeSort` and `BubbleSort`.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][Implement Bubble Sort](testBubbleSort)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Date>)` in the class `BubbleSort`. Make sure to follow the Bubble Sort algorithm exactly.

2. [task][Implement Merge Sort](testMergeSort)
Implement the method `performSort(List<Date>)` in the class `MergeSort`. Make sure to follow the Merge Sort algorithm exactly.

### Part 2: Strategy Pattern

We want the application to apply different algorithms for sorting a `List` of `Date` objects.
Use the strategy pattern to select the right sorting algorithm at runtime.

**You have the following tasks:**

1. [task][SortStrategy Interface](testSortStrategyInterface, testSortStrategyMethods)
Create a `SortStrategy` interface and adjust the sorting algorithms so that they implement this interface.

2. [task][Context Class](testContextClass, testContextMethods)
Create and implement a `Context` class following the below class diagram

3. [task][Context Policy](testPolicyClass, testPolicyConfigure, testPolicySelection)
Create and implement a `Policy` class following the below class diagram with a simple configuration mechanism:

    1. [task][Select MergeSort](testSelectMergeSort, testPolicyMerge)
    Select `MergeSort` when the List has more than 10 dates.

    2. [task][Select BubbleSort](testSelectBubbleSort, testPolicyBubble)
    Select `BubbleSort` when the List has less or equal 10 dates.

4. Complete the `Client` class which demonstrates switching between two strategies at runtime.

@startuml

class Client {
}

class Policy {
  <color:testsColor(testPolicySelection)>+configure()</color>
}

class Context {
  <color:testsColor(testContextClass)>-dates: List<Date></color>
  <color:testsColor(testContextMethods)>+sort()</color>
}

interface SortStrategy {
  <color:testsColor(testSortStrategyMethods)>+performSort(List<Date>)</color>
}

class BubbleSort {
  <color:testsColor(testBubbleSort)>+performSort(List<Date>)</color>
}

class MergeSort {
  <color:testsColor(testMergeSort)>+performSort(List<Date>)</color>
}

MergeSort -up-|> SortStrategy #testsColor(testSelectMergeSort)
BubbleSort -up-|> SortStrategy #testsColor(testSelectBubbleSort)
Policy -right-> Context #testsColor(testPolicySelection): context
Context -right-> SortStrategy #testsColor(testContextMethods): sortAlgorithm
Client .down.> Policy
Client .down.> Context

hide empty fields
hide empty methods

@enduml

### Part 3: Optional Challenges

(These are not tested)

1. Create a new class `QuickSort` that implements `SortStrategy` and implement the Quick Sort algorithm.

2. Make the method `performSort(List<Dates>)` generic, so that other objects can also be sorted by the same method.
   **Hint:** Have a look at Java Generics and the interface `Comparable`.

3. Think about a useful decision in `Policy` when to use the new `QuickSort` algorithm.

### Part 4: Harder Requirements

To increase the difficulty, you must also make the solution robust against edge cases.

**Additional tasks:**

1. [task][BubbleSort Null Input](testBubbleSortNullInput)
   `performSort(null)` must throw an `IllegalArgumentException`.

2. [task][BubbleSort Empty List](testBubbleSortEmpty)
   Sorting an empty list must leave the list unchanged and must not throw.

3. [task][MergeSort Null Input](testMergeSortNullInput)
   `performSort(null)` must throw an `IllegalArgumentException`.

4. [task][MergeSort Empty List](testMergeSortEmpty)
   Sorting an empty list must leave the list unchanged and must not throw.

5. [task][Context No Strategy](testContextNoStrategy)
   Calling `Context.sort()` when no `SortStrategy` has been configured must throw an `IllegalStateException`.

6. [task][Policy Null Dates](testPolicyNullDates)
   `Policy.configure()` must throw an `IllegalArgumentException` if the `Context` contains a `null` dates list.

These additional tests ensure that your implementation correctly handles invalid and boundary inputs, making the exercise considerably harder.
